Event Clock on staggered time grids

Source: R/measure.R
event_clock_staggered.Rd

With intraday prices, the measured clock depends on how often you sample: very fine sampling picks up bid-ask bounce and stale quotes, coarse sampling throws information away. A staggered grid estimate samples the price every interval minutes (the last price at or before each grid point) and repeats this for every possible starting offset of the grid; the estimator is applied to each grid separately and the results are averaged. This uses all the data while keeping the chosen sampling frequency — the construction behind the working paper's 30-, 60-, and 120-minute clocks.

Usage

event_clock_staggered(
  x,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  interval = 60,
  methods = "rv",
  offset_step = NULL,
  max_offsets = 60,
  trunc_sd = ec_default_params()$trunc_sd,
  scale_fn = stats::mad,
  clip = NULL
)

Arguments

x

An event_prices object (see as_event_prices()), or a data.frame coercible to one.

from

Valuation date/time (default: first observation).

to

One or more horizon dates/times (default: last observation = full sample). Names are used as horizon labels.

interval

Sampling interval in minutes (default 60).

methods

Character vector of estimator variants; see Details.

offset_step

Spacing of the grid offsets in minutes (default: the median spacing of the observations).

max_offsets

Maximum number of offset grids (default 60).

trunc_sd

Numeric, truncation threshold in robust standard deviations (default 3).

scale_fn

Function computing the robust scale of the increments for truncated (default stats::mad()).

clip

Numeric length-2 clipping bounds for q before the log-odds transform; defaults to the bounds stored in x.

Value

A tibble with one row per horizon and method: market_id, from, to, horizon, interval_min, n_offsets, n_incr (average increments per grid), method, A (average over grids), and A_min, A_max (range over grids).

Details

Each method is applied within each offset grid before averaging, so largest1 removes the largest move of every grid separately and bipower uses neighbors on the same grid — matching the paper's "largest-move exclusion in each staggered grid". Grid offsets run in steps of offset_step minutes (default: the data's median spacing), capped at max_offsets grids. Choose an interval no finer than the data's own spacing; otherwise repeated prices create zero increments. For daily data use sample_every in event_clock() or ec_signature() instead.

See also

ec_signature() for the full sampling-frequency profile.

Examples

data(polymarket2024)
ep <- as_event_prices(polymarket2024)
event_clock_staggered(ep, interval = 120, methods = c("rv", "largest1"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   market_id from                to                  horizon         interval_min
#>   <chr>     <dttm>              <dttm>              <chr>                  <dbl>
#> 1 NA        2024-06-01 00:00:03 2024-11-05 23:00:02 2024-11-05 23:…          120
#> 2 NA        2024-06-01 00:00:03 2024-11-05 23:00:02 2024-11-05 23:…          120
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: n_offsets <int>, n_incr <dbl>, method <chr>, A <dbl>,
#> #   A_min <dbl>, A_max <dbl>
